n
For z ̸= 1 on the unit circle, the partial sums of z are bounded by the finite geometric-sum
formula. Dirichlet's test with 1/n ↓ 0 gives convergence. At z = 1 the series is harmonic
and diverges. At every boundary point its absolute-value series is the harmonic series, so
none of this boundary convergence is absolute.

question.text:
After removing the singularity at z = 1, what is the radius of convergence about zero of (z −
1)/[(z − 1)(z − 3)]?
(A) 4 (B) 3 (C) 2 (D) 1 (E) ∞

solution.text:
The analytic extension is 1/(z − 3). The apparent singularity at 1 is removable and does not
limit its Taylor series; the actual pole at 3 gives radius 3.
